rule.description: A function whose body contains near-complete duplicates of one or more still-defined functions elsewhere in the package: the body of each absorbed helper survives as inlined fragments inside the owner while the original helper remains, so the owner re-implements sub-method logic instead of calling it.
rule.definition: Every callable under the certipy package is reduced to a normalized token stream (identifier names and literal values collapse, control keywords and attribute names are preserved, nested function bodies reduce to a DEF marker). Exact 8-token gram seeds anchor a candidate owner against smaller candidate sources (owner at least twice the source's token count); seeds chain monotonically with bounded gaps, surviving the drift from owner-specific statements interleaved between inlined fragments. A (owner, source) pair is absorption evidence when the surviving dense chains cover at least 75% of the source's tokens, occupy at least 50 matched tokens, include control flow, and stay at least 65% dense over their spans. An owner is reported once per absorbed source when at least two distinct sources are absorbed and the total matched material reaches 200 tokens. One message is emitted per absorbing (owner, source) pair, anchored on the owner function.

checks.description: Detect functions that subsume near-complete copies of still-existing helper implementations instead of delegating to them, with enough absorbed material across enough distinct sources to have folded several sub-methods into one body.
checks.detected_relation: owner function -> absorbed body of a live helper function
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The owner re-implements the sub-method's own implementation inline, so the live helper and its inlined copy must both be understood, compared, and kept in sync; this is the deeply inlined method smell rather than ordinary shared-shape code.

matches.evidence: Request.request near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.certificate.create_csr: the CSR construction pipeline from key generation through subject build, CRI extension assembly, request signature guard and DER dump is reproduced inline (first inlined fragment at line 1433) while create_csr remains defined and exported.

Request.request near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.certificate.create_on_behalf_of: the CMC request-attribute set with requester name, EKU attribute, message digest and SignedData wrapping is reproduced inline while create_on_behalf_of remains defined.

Request.request near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.certificate.create_renewal: the renewal CMC wrapping including renewal-certificate attribute, digest computation and signer-info assembly is reproduced inline while create_renewal remains defined and exported.

Request.request near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.req.handle_request_response: the issued-certificate handling including identity extraction, SID logging, output-filename derivation and PFX assembly is reproduced inline while handle_request_response remains defined and is still imported by certipy.commands.relay.

Request.request near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.certificate.create_csr_attributes: the enrollment attribute assembly for SAN entries, SID security extension, renewal hints and application policies is reproduced inline while create_csr_attributes remains defined.

Forge.build_new_certificate near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.certificate.create_pfx: the key-type validation guard, legacy PFX encryption builder and serialize_key_and_certificates call are reproduced inline while create_pfx remains defined (and is still called by other Forge methods).

Forge.build_new_certificate near-duplicates the still-defined Forge.create_subject_alternative_names: the UPN/DNS/URL extension-building loop is reproduced inline while create_subject_alternative_names remains defined on the same class.

Find._process_template_properties near-duplicates the still-defined Find._process_template_flags: the template flag enumeration loop is reproduced inline while _process_template_flags remains defined on the same class.

Find._process_template_properties near-duplicates the still-defined Find._process_template_policies: the application-policies and EKU reporting logic is reproduced inline while _process_template_policies remains defined on the same class.

Find._process_template_properties near-duplicates the still-defined Find._process_template_validity: the validity-period reconstruction logic is reproduced inline while _process_template_validity remains defined on the same class.

The cert command's entry near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.certificate.create_pfx: the key-type validation dump and PKCS12 encryption builder are reproduced inline while create_pfx remains defined and exported.

The cert command's entry near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.commands.cert.write_output at both of its rendering sites: the binary/text mode selection, open-with-error-handling and stdout writing are reproduced inline twice while write_output remains defined in the same module.

The cert command's entry near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.commands.cert.load_certificate_file: the guarded file read with per-error logging is reproduced inline while load_certificate_file remains defined in the same module.

The cert command's entry near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.commands.cert.load_key_file: the guarded file read with per-error logging is reproduced inline while load_key_file remains defined in the same module.

HttpxNtlmAuth.retry_with_auth near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.ntlm.compute_response: the NTLMv2 response computation including AV-pair construction, SPN derivation, timestamp and proof calculation is reproduced inline while compute_response remains defined.

HttpxNtlmAuth.retry_with_auth near-duplicates the still-defined certipy.lib.channel_binding.get_channel_binding_data_from_response: the EPA channel-binding hash extraction from the TLS response is reproduced inline while the channel_binding helper remains defined and exported.

excluded: Pre-existing structural sibling families that share scaffolding but absorb nothing (CA.issue/CA.deny/CA.enable and the get_*_properties / get_*_output_for_csv / *_has_vulnerable_acl groups in commands/find.py, the request/retrieve pair on the RPC and DCOM interfaces, the create_renewal/create_on_behalf_of CMC tail in lib/certificate.py, and the CASecurity/ActiveDirectorySecurity _parse_aces twins): they fall under the rule's coverage, density or multi-source requirements and are intentionally outside this case's smell.

Sub-floor absorbed material: the inline copies of certipy's parse_certificate/parse_key PEM/DER fallbacks in commands/cert.py, and the inline key-archival wrapper in Request.request, which rewrites the transitive MS key-blob formatting so heavily that its similarity to create_key_archival sits below the single-pair coverage floor. Their absorbed fragments exist in the owner but count toward no owner.

Nested helper functions defined inside the function they serve (for example get_dce_rpc's _try_binding/_try_dyn or Find._save_output's prepare_for_json): contained helpers are a normal composition idiom and are excluded by construction from both the owner's and the helper's stream.
